findings.source_quote: οὐκ ἔστι γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ὡς οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ μνησικακοῦντες, ἀλλ᾽ αὐτὸς ἀμνησίκακός ἐστι
findings.english_quote: The Greek uses the bearing-a-grudge / not-bearing-a-grudge pair. The retained remember-wrongs wording describes this contrast; bear a grudge is an alternative idiomatic rendering.
findings.issue: Footnote j incorrectly identifies the simplified edition’s retained wording. Its main text already uses “hold grudges” and “He holds no grudge,” not remember-wrongs wording. The note consequently presents the main-text idiom as merely an alternative and misreports this edition’s translation choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed note for fresh review: “The Greek uses a bearing-a-grudge / not-bearing-a-grudge pair. ‘Hold grudges’ and ‘holds no grudge’ render that contrast here; the standard edition uses ‘remember wrongs’ and ‘does not remember wrongs.’” No main-text change is needed for this finding.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all twelve paragraphs of the supplied working Greek. Both preserve the difficult assertions, conditions, negations, personification, and closing mental condition, and follow the current servant and contextual repentance policies. The standard edition is acceptable within this review’s scope; the simplified edition needs correction of one inaccurate shared note. Stated witness alternatives were assessed as editorial disclosures, not independently verified readings. This review does not certify unseen editions, manuscript handwriting, restoration provenance, or exhaustive collation. The proposed note remains subject to fresh review.
